newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela farmers protest over cheap imports.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela farmers protest over cheap imports.

text.p: Farmers in central Venezuela rallied peacefully Tuesday against cheap wheat, corn and sorghum imports and asked the government to guarantee set minimum prices for their produce.
The farmers are only trying to "defend their right to life and work," Portugesa state governor Ivan Colmenares told local radio and television.

But Eduardo Gomez, Vice President of Venezuela's Chamber of Agro-industrialists said "local prices were far above imported prices." Faced with high costs and a strong currency that favors imports, farmers say they can only get 90 bolivars per kilo of sorghum whereas the price should be nearer double that.
Protesting farmers' first hit Venezuelan newspaper headlines in March when Portugesa state, in the hot flat plainslands of central Venezuela, banned agricultural imports.
